issues.legal_issue: A mutation decision made after consolidation proposals became final does not bar a later civil suit to determine title when the governing law provided no further consolidation proceeding for adjudicating that title.
material_facts: The original landholder died after the consolidation proposals had become final but before the village was denotified.
The claimant’s application to be recorded as heir was dealt with as a mutation matter, and the consolidation authorities found that he was not an adopted son.
Under the law then in force, once the proposals had become final, the consolidation authorities had no provision available to adjudicate the new succession claim as a matter of title.
After consolidation ended, the claimant brought a civil suit seeking recognition of his adoption and title to the deceased’s property.
issues.conclusion: The earlier mutation decision did not adjudicate title and did not bar the civil suit under res judicata or the statutory bar to civil jurisdiction. The High Court’s dismissal was set aside, and the case was remitted for decision on the adoption issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 49 of the Uttar Pradesh Consolidation of Holdings Act, as it stood before the 1963 amendment, civil jurisdiction was barred for matters that were or could have been adjudicated in consolidation proceedings. Res judicata may also apply to a consolidation authority’s adjudication of title (Raj Lakshmi Dasi v. Banamali Sen). But mutation proceedings do not decide rights or title, and after the proposals became final the authorities lacked power under the then-existing law to adjudicate a later succession claim as title. The Court approved Smt. Natho v. Board of Revenue and followed Suba Singh v. Mahendra Singh on the distinction between mutation and title adjudication.

predicates.civil_suit_seeking_title_adjudication: A party brings a civil suit seeking determination of title to property.
predicates.succession_claim_arose_after_proposals_f: The event giving rise to a succession claim occurred after the consolidation proposals had become final.
predicates.prior_decision_was_mutation_only: The earlier authority dealt with the claimant’s request to be recorded as successor as a mutation matter, rather than adjudicating title.
predicates.no_post_finality_title_proceeding_was_av: The governing framework provided no further proceeding before the consolidation authority to adjudicate the later claim as a matter of title after the proposals became final.

issues.definition: When a civil title suit follows a later-arising succession claim and the earlier decision was only a mutation decision, with no available post-finality title proceeding, the earlier decision does not bar the suit.

issues.legal_issue: Under the amended consolidation framework, a later-arising change affecting rights recorded in the revised records may be adjudicated by consolidation authorities as a matter of title.
material_facts: The Court explained that the 1963 amendment added a procedure for matters involving later changes or transactions affecting rights or interests recorded in revised records.
That procedure applied to causes of action arising after the earlier consolidation proceedings had begun and before the consolidation proceedings were brought to an end.
The amended procedure applied the procedures used for adjudicating rights and title to the later-arising matter.
issues.conclusion: Under the amended framework, adjudication of a later-arising cause concerning recorded rights amounts to adjudication of rights and title.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Uttar Pradesh Consolidation of Holdings Act, added by the 1963 amendment, permits matters concerning later changes or transactions affecting rights or interests in revised records to be raised before the consolidation authority before the proceedings end. Sections 7 to 11 apply to the hearing and decision of those matters, making the resulting decision an adjudication of rights and title. The Court distinguished the earlier framework and approved Smt. Natho v. Board of Revenue on the prior law’s limits.

predicates.later_rights_change_consolidation_case: A matter concerning a later change in rights is brought before a consolidation authority.
predicates.later_change_affects_recorded_rights: The later change or transaction affects rights or interests already recorded in revised records.
predicates.cause_arose_after_initial_claim_stage: The cause of action arose after the initial stage for raising claims about rights had begun or was underway.
predicates.proceedings_remained_open: The matter was raised before the consolidation proceedings were brought to an end.

issues.definition: When a later change affecting recorded rights is raised before consolidation proceedings end and the full title-adjudication procedure applies, the resulting decision is a title adjudication.
